title: Kevin Vallejos hopes highlight UFC Qatar KO gets Alexander Volkanovski's attention
text:
UFC Qatar: Kevin Vallejos aims to get Alex Volkanovski's attention Videos Blue Corner Schedule Results Rankings Fighters A.S. 1980-2025 💙 Newsletter UFC Kevin Vallejos hopes highlight UFC Qatar KO gets Alexander Volkanovski's attention
 Farah Hannoun Mike Bohn MMA Junkie Nov. 19, 2026, 5:01 p.m. ET Kevin Vallejos has one goal at UFC Fight Night 294: Lure Alexander Volkanovski into a title fight.
 Vallejos (18-1 MMA, 4-0 UFC) meets former champ Aljamain Sterling (26-5 MMA, 18-5 UFC) in Saturday's co-main event ( Paramount+ ) at ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar.
 UFC featherweight champion Volkanovski (29-4 MMA, 16-3 UFC) has acknowledged Vallejos as a contender – especially if he can get past Sterling, whom he views as the most worthy challenger.
 "By me beating Aljamain Sterling the way that I will, I think that the highlight is going to reach Volkanovski, and I feel like it's going to excite him to want to prove that he can fight and beat the new generation of fighter, which I think I would represent," Vallejos told MMA Junkie through an interpreter. "So, I think I would get the opportunity with Volkanovski. If it's not Volkanovski because he decides to move up, it would be also amazing to be able to finally get my rematch with Jean Silva for a vacant title."
 Although the matchup is considered striker vs. grappler, knockout artist Vallejos knows Sterling is tricky on the feet.
 "Aljamain Sterling is a good striker, 100 percent," Vallejos said. "I think that his awkward style makes it difficult to predict. He's an unpredictable fighter, and he's very awkward in the way he does things. But he didn't get to the place he is by being just a grappler, but I do think because he's such an amazing grappler, that probably stands out more than his striking does."
 Vallejos has 13 knockouts to his name and has no doubt that he can add Sterling to that long list.
 "That's one of my advantages: I'm unpredictable," Vallejos said. "I've had much less cage time than he has, but at the same time, I think I have a lot of experience, and I'm ready for this being that I've trained everyday, which at the end of the day, the most important thing is what you do at the gym, and I always do that. I think that my biggest advantage is also that with him, just like anyone else, I have the ability to put anyone's lights out in any round so. That makes me very dangerous as a fighter, as well."
